title: A Comprehensive Environmental Impact Analysis of a Wastewater Treatment Plant in Southern China by Life Cycle Assessment
content:
Life cycle assessment of a wastewater treatment plant in southern China showed that biological treatment dominated most environmental burdens, whereas effluent discharge drove eutrophication. Increasing the reuse rate of reclaimed water can significantly reduce toxicity-related and resource consumption-related environmental impacts.


ABSTRACT

This study used the life cycle assessment (LCA) to analyze the environmental burdens of a municipal wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) with a designed capacity of 30,000 m3/day in southern China. The CML-Baseline method was applied to evaluate 11 environmental impact categories, and the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) method was integrated to quantify greenhouse gas emissions. In addition, water reuse scenarios, sensitivity analysis, and Monte Carlo simulation were employed to assess the potential for environmental improvement and the robustness of the results. The results indicated that the biological treatment stage was the primary environmental hotspot for abiotic depletion potential (fossil fuels) (ADP-ff), global warming potential (GWP), and marine aquatic ecotoxicity potential (MAETP), contributing 63.3%, 51.8%, and 63.0%, respectively. The effluent discharge stage contributed 75.1% of the ozone depletion potential (ODP) and 90.2% of the eutrophication potential (EP), whereas the sludge disposal stage contributed 96.7% of the terrestrial ecotoxicity potential (TETP). Greenhouse gas accounting showed that N2O accounted for 66% of the direct greenhouse gas impact, whereas the biological treatment stage contributed 62% of the indirect greenhouse gas emissions, indicating that the biological nitrogen removal process and operational electricity consumption were the key control nodes for direct and indirect greenhouse gas mitigation, respectively. Water reuse could reduce environmental impacts when no additional electricity was consumed. However, under the condition of a 75% reuse rate and an additional electricity consumption of 1.00 kWh/m3, the GWP, acidification potential (AP), and MAETP increased by 86.2%, 87.0%, and 133.5%, respectively, compared with the no-reuse scenario. Sensitivity analysis demonstrated that resource consumption-related indicators were most responsive to changes in electricity consumption, and the Monte Carlo simulation confirmed the stability of the model results. The findings provided empirical guidance and a reference for environmental assessment and mitigation strategy formulation in WWTPs.
